subject: General Science
title: The Periodic Table

outcomes.text: examine electron arrangement of an atom of an element,
classify elements into groups and periods of the periodic table,
explain the stability and electron affinity of atoms of elements,
describe ion formation for the first 20 elements of the periodic table,
formulate chemical formula of common compounds,
write balanced equations of chemical reactions,
appreciate the importance of the structure of the atom in the development of the periodic table.

content: Classification of the first twenty elements of the periodic table
Electron configuration of atoms of elements
inquiry_questions: How are elements arranged in the periodic table?
suggested_learning_experiences: Carry out activities to review the concepts of the structure of an atom, atomic number, mass number and electron arrangement of atoms of selected elements.
Arrange the first 20 elements using similarities in their electron arrangements.
Discuss with peers the order adopted in developing the periodic table (the periodic law).
Discuss with peers how atoms of elements acquire stability (losing or gaining electrons) relating to the atom’s ability to attain the positive or negative charge (cations and anions).
Discuss the unreactive nature of noble gases.
Draw dot (.) and cross (x) diagrams to illustrate ion formation for the first 20 elements of the periodic table.
Discuss with peers on how to determine the valency and oxidation numbers of elements and radicals (ammonium ion, sulphate, nitrate, hydroxide, carbonate, phosphate, hydrogen carbonate).
Write chemical formula of common compounds using valencies of elements and radicals.
Use valencies of elements and radicals to balance chemical equations.
Watch animations and simulations on ion formation and atomicity of gases using digital devices.
Project: Model electron configuration of any five elements of the periodic table (1–20) using locally available materials.
Project: Make a chart of common substances that are made from the elements and radicals (include names and formulae).
coreCompetencies:
Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: as the learner sorts and arranges the first twenty elements of the periodic table according to their similarities.
Creativity and Imagination: as the learner models the electron configuration of any five elements of the periodic table using locally available materials.
values:
Respect: as the learner recognises and respects the input of every group member as they discuss how to determine the valency and oxidation numbers of elements and radicals.
Unity: as the learner takes turns in playing roles when drawing dot (.) and cross (x) diagrams to illustrate ion formation for atoms of elements of the periodic table.
Responsibility: as the learner uses digital devices appropriately to watch simulations and animations on ion formation.
pcis:
Life skills (Problem solving skills): as the learner arranges the first twenty elements of the periodic table into groups and periods.
Financial literacy: as the learner uses locally available materials as a way of minimising the expenses when modelling the electron configuration of any five elements of the periodic table.
